title: Hampton orchestra personnel, Trummy Young and the Cotton Club job
summary: He recalls Country Allen and a compliment from Trummy Young, and that the Culver City Cotton Club job lasted only about four weeks.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: I see. Well in Lionel Hampton's orchestra, how long were you actually with that orchestra, and how many other trombones did he have at that time?

There was a, there was a fellow by the name of Country Allen. I remember he was in there. And during those -- a, let's see, what a, what a -- I'm gettin' my, I'm gettin' my names and my years mixed up because at one time a, when I was with Charlie Echols, during those years a, in, in came -- walks in a trombone player by the name of Trummy Young, who is the famous Trummy Young of today. And a, he heard me play, and he, he complimented me, and it sounded nice coming from a great musician. He was something, you know. Cause of the years he put in with Jimmy Lunceford -- he started out with Earl Hines, you know. Oh, I just had a wonderful time in, in, in California up until I left.
I see. Um, you played an awful lot. I guess Hampton's orchestra played a, a very frequently during that time ,or were there periods where there were long

No, we were, we were playing at the Cotton Club in Culver City. This is a steady job, and I had a car then. I would drive in from, from Los Angeles to Culver City, and we'd play. I wasn't, I wasn't there no longer than about four weeks, and after that, why a, they changed hands. The band left. . . they went into the -- I think it was the name of the Frolics on May Street in L.A. I played with another band after that.
